text:
Jin K: FYI I spun up a repro for last week's latency storm. pattern: many small requests allocate transient activations, KV cache growth + a hot pinned tensor blocks eviction and we hit device OOM. had a different idea for a recovery surface: a memory admission controller + an evictor-broker.
Becca M: can you sketch what you mean by "admission controller"?
Jin K: short: instead of only reacting on OOM, we gate new allocations when hotset + predicted growth crosses a threshold. admission controller returns ALLOW / DELAY / REJECT with a short retry-after. DELAY lets requests queue briefly and triggers background reclaim.
Theo R: interesting. that would prevent the cliff where many requests simultaneously push past capacity. how do we pick retry-after?
Jin K: adaptive: base on current reclaim rate and per-tenant SLA. start with 20-100ms and adapt using EWMA of reclaim throughput.
Becca M: where does evictor-broker fit?
Jin K: broker is a small coordinating layer between runtime and allocator that sequences non-conflicting reclaim actions across tenants. when admission controller decides to DELAY, broker asks tenants for reclaimable candidates, applies ordered actions (unpin KV, compress, async migrate), and reports reclaimed bytes back.
Anita V: sounds like the oom-warning idea but elevated to admission-time instead of only on failure. any tenant-side changes needed?
Theo R: yes tenants should expose reclaim handlers but also a small SDK helper: register_reclaim_handler(priority, callback). callback returns reclaimed_bytes and optionally a set of async futures for long-running checkpointing. broker waits for short window then proceeds.
Becca M: security / isolation note: broker must not let a tenant's handler block others; we should cap per-tenant reclaim time and bytes. also handlers run in sandboxed execution context.
Jin K: agreed. proposed flow:
1) allocation request arrives -> admission controller computes delta
2) if ALLOW -> allocate
3) if DELAY -> broker starts reclaim round, signal tenants (with per-tenant token and budget)
4) wait up to reclaim_window_ms, aggregate reclaimed, retry allocation
5) if still insufficient -> either REJECT or fall back to CPU path based on policy

Theo R: where to keep metadata? need per-buffer annotations: is_pinned, compressible_lvl, recompute_cost_hint, tenant_priority. allocation API must accept these.
Becca M: we should normalize tags: compressible: low/med/high, recompute_cost_ms, checkpointable:true/false. that lets scorer be simpler.
Anita V: rollout concerns: landing admission controller changes on serving path adds p99 overhead risk. we need microbenching. Jin, can you run a benchmark comparing path with ALLOW check vs without? target <0.5% p99 overhead.
Jin K: will do. also plan a lightweight fast-path: if free_memory > watermark, skip controller entirely. only pay cost near capacity.
Theo R: eviction ordering: broker should prefer actions that don't increase cross-tenant interference. ordering proposal: tenant-local soft-unpin, tenant-local compress, tenant-local checkpoint-async, cross-tenant demote (opt-in), fallback-cpu.
Becca M: metric set: admission_denials, average_delay_ms, reclaimed_per_round, cross_tenant_evictions. also a histogram of retry counts.
Anita V: policy knobs in runtime config and per-tenant overrides. default conservative: no cross-tenant, max_delay_ms: 200, reclaim_window_ms: 120. enterprise can set allow_preempt true.
Theo R: test ideas: 1) synthetic churn with pinned tensor that only becomes free after checkpoint delay -> ensure broker's async wait recovers without big tail; 2) adversarial tenant that always refuses to reclaim -> ensure fairness and no starvation.
Becca M: implementation split: Jin -> admission controller + metrics, Theo -> broker + allocator glue, Anita -> rollout and policy docs. I'll own sandboxing/handler security model.
ops-bot: canary: admission-controller-v1 deployed to pool-canary-5 :white_check_mark:
Jin K: pushed initial PR for tags & SDK helpers; will add benchmark numbers tomorrow.
Anita V: good work. please put sequence diagram + API signatures in a short RFC and link to the canary results thread. closing for now.
